d: Burbo's Tavern. On a board embedded in the wall, they hang oil orchards and amphorae of wine: other amphorae scattered on the ground. On a bench are thrown in bulk the pallii of the young Patrizi, who around another play at the dice; while, on the opposite side, some Gladiators drink and cianchiano among them cheerfully. It is the dawn already forwarded. Three or four lamps placed around on the wall painted in bright colors, send a rest of light. Among the young Patrizi, Glaucus, Clodius and Sallustio: later Burbo going and coming wine or other.
Nidia, then Burbo and sayings.
Burbo indi Arbace.
Room of Jone richly decorated. The doors are closed by purple curtains and walls adorned with paintings: one of the doors puts in the garden. Jone alone.
Arbace and dictated.
Tell us, Nidia and sayings.

Portico which gives access to the gardens of Jone's house. In the center of the garden, an elegant fountain, and here and there oddly arranged, some marble statues. It is near the evening. On one side the apartments internally illuminated. Nidia, leaning on a column, is immersed in deep sadness, while listening to the following:
Burbo and saying.
Glauco indi Jone.
Invite, Schia among which Nidia, Dirce and sayings, in Arbace.

Piazza in Pompeii; on the one hand the house of Arbace before whose majestic vestibule rise two huge sphinxes: adjacent to the same, the temple of Isis. It is night; the serene and starry sky; the market is still populated and lively. Under small curtains are the Sellers of fish and fruit, whose voices alternate with those of the Flowers.
Arbace leaves his home. A priest of Isis who followed him keeps himself apart in a respectful attitude.
Jone and Nidia.

Magnificent room in the house of Arbace. Some lamps of wonderful work hanging from the ceiling, send a pale and mysterious light. Precious paintings adorn the walls, and Greek sculptures are arranged to turn on granite pedestals. In the bottom the simulacrum of Isis, behind which stretches a curtain of purple. Side doors. Arbace only, at the end of the Ethiopian Schiavo and Jone.
Glauco followed by Nidia and some of her friends, including Sallustio, Dirce and Schiarca of Jone, Priests, Slaves of Arbace, among whom the Ethiopian, Burbo and sayings.

Large road of Pompeii: on the one hand the outside of the amphitheatre: on the other, in some distance, the sea. Citizens richly dressed, some of them with followers of Schiavi: people of Pompeii and of the neighbouring countries clutter the scene heading to the amphitheatre, whose doors are open. Various among the People hold Burbo, and they tighten with it in conversation.
Glauco, Littori, Soldiers, etc., other People and sayings.
Sallustio and Nidia.
Jone, go to Arbace.
Jone alone.
Glauco, Nidia, Sallustio and Said People.
